leading_positions.synthesis: B041 (GLP-1 physiology and incretin therapies) with Drucker, Holst and Knudsen. These three members share the physiology-plus-translation framing, with Knudsen's protraction chemistry behind liraglutide and semaglutide treated as the step that made the discovery a medicine. They do not fully agree on how firmly to hold it: Perlmann and Svenningsson explicitly accept that Drucker, Holst and Mojsov is the cleaner basic-science trio if the committee decides the discovery strand alone is prize-worthy, and El-Manira calls the Knudsen versus Mojsov choice a judgement call on which colleagues may differ. Their citations are worded around physiology and its translation.

B041 with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. These three members anchor the citation in the discovery of GLP-1 physiology and the identification of the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) form, with the drug class as its consequence. They share the concern that Habener is absent from the supplied names and that Knudsen is excluded. Linnarsson holds his choice with only moderate confidence and names Drucker, Holst and Knudsen as the more defensible fallback if the Mojsov priority question cannot be resolved; Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius both state that Knudsen is a plausible additional name or alternative.

areas_of_agreement: All six members rank B041 first and propose exactly Drucker and Holst for two of the three places; the only difference in B041 is the third name (Knudsen in three configurations, Mojsov in three).
All six members list B035 (CAR-T) as an alternative to B041; the other alternatives named are B033 (El-Manira, Perlmann, Svenningsson), B034 (Linnarsson), B007 (Sandberg) and B004 (Wahren-Herlenius).

All six members describe B041 as mature, independently confirmed in large randomized trials (diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal outcomes), and state that unanimity in opening rankings is not itself the argument.
No member discloses a specific conflict with any shortlisted candidate, and no member proposes a recusal.
Every member who comments on B033 accepts that any three-name selection from six credited names is contestable.
scientific_disputes: Whether the B041 citation should reward the physiology and identification of the hormone (Drucker, Holst, Mojsov), or physiology plus the drug-design step (Drucker, Holst, Knudsen), or whether the two strands deserve separate recognition. Several members flag that combining two physiologists with an industrial drug developer merges different kinds of achievement.

Whether a research-tool method such as B033 (optogenetics) meets the criterion of benefit to human health as strongly as a therapy. Perlmann treats methods-based impact as legitimate prize material, El-Manira (via Sandberg's summary) ranks it third while questioning the fit for a research tool, and Svenningsson asks the same question while describing clinical translation as only beginning.

Which fallback best represents a new conceptual step: CAR-T as a new therapeutic modality (B035), or BCR-ABL inhibition (B004) as the template for targeted kinase-inhibitor oncology. Wahren-Herlenius ranks B004 second; El-Manira asks her to justify placing it above B035.

Whether mechanism-driven basic science with modest clinical payoff (B042 unfolded protein response, B037 cGAS-STING), raised by Linnarsson and Perlmann, deserves consideration alongside therapies, and whether the B007 antisense platform's reach beyond a rare disease is yet shown.
attribution_disputes: B041: Mojsov's priority for identifying the active GLP-1(7-36) form is described as contested with the Habener group, and Habener is not on the supplied credited list. Three members name Mojsov, three name Knudsen, and the supplied material does not settle which third name is better supported.
B041: whether Knudsen's acylation-based protraction work was creative invention or routine development, and whether leaving her out under-values the step that put the therapy in patients.

B035: Sandberg proposes only June and Sadelain and treats Rosenberg as a foundational predecessor; El-Manira notes that Eshhar is absent from the credited list, and Linnarsson questions the completeness of the configuration because an originator of the chimeric receptor concept is missing. Whether the credited names are complete is unresolved.

B033: six credited names (Bamberg, Boyden, Deisseroth, Hegemann, Miesenboeck, Nagel) for three places; El-Manira, Perlmann and Svenningsson each state that any split leaves out significant contributors or is contestable.
B034: El-Manira raises the question of Zhou and the parallel development by two groups with commercial involvement, which blurs the credit boundary for the Lowy, Schiller and Frazer trio.
maturity_disputes: B041 is treated by all members as mature, but Perlmann questions whether the newest cardiovascular, renal and neurological indications need more follow-up before appearing in a citation, and Linnarsson notes that long-term safety is still being defined.
B033: Svenningsson and El-Manira describe clinical translation as only beginning, while Perlmann points to the method's broad adoption and early vision-restoration results.
B007: El-Manira ranks it below CAR-T and optogenetics because the disease is rare and the platform's broader reach is still being shown; Sandberg ranks it third as a clean mechanism-to-drug story.

B004: Wahren-Herlenius describes the case as mature and arguably overdue, with more than twenty years of survival data; El-Manira ranks B035 higher for conceptual novelty but calls the B004 maturity and attribution argument strong.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Svenningsson (chair) discloses postdoctoral work with Paul Greengard and about twenty co-authored works with Perlmann on dopamine neurons, Nurr1 and autophagy; no shortlisted candidate is connected, and he notes his neurology background in relation to B033.

Perlmann discloses nuclear-receptor co-authorship with Ronald Evans and KI collaborations including Johan Ericson, with Svenningsson and El-Manira as colleagues; none involves a shortlisted candidate.
El-Manira discloses a 2009 paper with Perlmann and a 2019 synthesis with Sten Grillner, and that B033 is in his general field without documented involvement with its credited names.

Sandberg discloses a field interest in RNA processing and splicing relevant to B007 and B042, and past co-authorship with Linnarsson and Jonas Frisen; no personal connection to credited candidates is stated.

Linnarsson and Wahren-Herlenius disclose no specific conflicts; Linnarsson notes shared KI affiliation and co-authorship, and Wahren-Herlenius notes no collaboration with credited GLP-1, CAR-T or BCR-ABL candidates.
questions_for_round2: For B041, should the third laureate alongside Drucker and Holst be Knudsen or Mojsov, and what in the supplied record establishes Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) form relative to the Habener group, who are not on the list?

Should a B041 citation cover both the physiological discovery and the long-acting drug development, and if so can one citation describe both with three names without misrepresenting either contribution, or does the committee prefer one strand and a distinct second achievement?
If B041 needs a second prize part or a fallback, which of B035, B004, B033 or B034 is best supported, and how should absent names (Eshhar for B035, Zhou for B034) affect that choice?

For B035, should the credited laureates be June, Sadelain and Rosenberg, or only June and Sadelain (Sandberg's position), and how much weight should Rosenberg's foundational role and the absence of Eshhar carry?

For B033, does a research-tool method with early clinical translation meet the criterion as strongly as a therapy, and if so which three of Bamberg, Boyden, Deisseroth, Hegemann, Miesenboeck and Nagel can be defended?
Wahren-Herlenius places B004 above B035 on clean attribution and maturity; El-Manira and others rank B035 higher as a new modality. What would each member need to see to move between these two?
summary.chair_observation: The round-1 files show full convergence on B041 as the lead candidate, split evenly three to three on the third laureate, and no explicit support in any preferred configuration for a second prize part. The open issues are the Knudsen versus Mojsov choice and the status of the Habener credit, the choice and credit of a fallback among B035, B004 and B033, and the unresolved credit questions in the alternatives. These are stated here as the members' own positions; no member's statement has been altered.
